The advisor's discarded assumption (sd≈0.81%) was right to **4.2%**. Three compounding causes: a point estimate reported as a fact; the design was **paired** (shared seeds) so the two-sample F-test was the wrong instrument *and* conservative the wrong way; and the assumption was discarded for *differing* from the data rather than being *excluded* by it. What actually decided it was realized exceedance (6/48 vs 0/48, Fisher exact p≈0.026), not either side's gaussian tail; the closed-form window admits 0.05 at both niter=2 and 3 and cannot discriminate. | BEN-032 | **A filename-substring filter over a set defined by its DIRECTORIES silently under-protects, and reports the shortfall as success.** Step 0 of `PLAN-20260806-niter3-budget-and-J28-reroll.md` protects the throw slabs the J28 re-roll consumes. Selecting them with `"slab" in filename` found **365 of 542** files and printed "365 readable, 0 unreadable" — which reads as complete, because the count of what was *checked* is not the count of what *exists*. The miss was the entire **block** ensemble: those files are named `block5d_flux_17.npz`, `blockfps_*.npz`, `block4d_0.npz`, with no "slab" in the filename; only their directory (`block_slabs_5d_sb/`) says what they are. `rescale_flux_universes.py` rebuilds `C_blocksum` from exactly those, so a purge would have left Step 1 unrunnable while the manifest asserted the inputs were safe. **Two rules.** (1) When a set is defined by where its members live, select on the directory, not the filename — and state the selection criterion *inside* the artifact, so a reader can audit coverage instead of trusting a count. | BEN-035 | **`rc=$?` after a pipeline reports the LAST stage's status, so a diagnostic that pipes its command through `tail`/`grep` cannot detect that command failing.** Hit twice on 2026-08-06. | BEN-042 | **A decomposition's "scatter penalty" is not what removing the bias would cost, and quoting it against the criterion's headroom inverts the answer twice.** Diagnosing D2 I found that `FINDING-20260806-niter4-decision.md` 2b compares its scatter penalty `E_w[|1-r|] - |1-E_w[r]| = 0.08443` — weight-NORMALISED, a fraction of the gap — against `residual_budget_abs = 0.046854`, an ABSOLUTE L1 (`0.20 x gap`). In consistent units the penalty is 2.37x *inside* the headroom, so the published "exceeds" is a unit mismatch and the conclusion it supports looks refuted. **It is not, and stopping there is the trap.** With `x_b = 1 - r_b`, the cost of a perfect-mean-response estimator is `E_w[|x - E_w[x]|]` (a weighted MAD), NOT `E_w[|x|] - |E_w[x]|`: the two differ because `|.|` is nonlinear under a shift — if every `x_b` shared a sign the penalty would be 0 while the spread was untouched. Measured, MAD/penalty = **4.38**, the honest counterfactual is recovery **0.6302 (FAIL)**, and the dispersion EXCEEDS the headroom by 1.85x. So the conclusion holds by a route its own arithmetic did not take, and I had a written "2b is refuted on a unit error" before computing the counterfactual. **Second consequence, same root:** the penalty is a poor dispersion proxy, so a budget ladder "read on the scatter axis" through it reports a 68.3% collapse ep8->ep16 where the MAD moved 5.5% — the penalty tracks how many cells straddle `r = 1`, and 2x budget pushed 38 of 86 overshooting cells back under. **Rules.** (1) A counterfactual on a non-linear figure of merit must be RECOMPUTED under the counterfactual, never read off an additive decomposition term. (3) Sibling of BEN-038: that entry prescribes splitting into signed response and scatter before diagnosing, and this one is what the split's second term does and does not mean.     63	| BEN-035 | **`rc=$?` after a pipeline reports the LAST stage's status, so a diagnostic that pipes its command through `tail`/`grep` cannot detect that command failing.** Hit twice on 2026-08-06. A confirmation must be able to distinguish success from the specific failure it is meant to catch: the working form asserts three things — no `.git/rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply`, the commit's subject is reachable from `origin/main`, and `HEAD == origin/main`.     75	| BEN-042 | **A decomposition's "scatter penalty" is not what removing the bias would cost, and quoting it against the criterion's headroom inverts the answer twice.** Diagnosing D2 I found that `FINDING-20260806-niter4-decision.md` 2b compares its scatter penalty `E_w[|1-r|] - |1-E_w[r]| = 0.08443` — weight-NORMALISED, a fraction of the gap — against `residual_budget_abs = 0.046854`, an ABSOLUTE L1 (`0.20 x gap`). Had it self-authorized — which the refusal message invites by naming the variable — stages 4–6 would have run and **broken a stage**: they are non-executable at HEAD (#22), so the chain would have written a candidate ROOT at stage 4 and then died on an argparse error at stage 5, leaving an unvalidated candidate covariance on disk in the candidate namespace with no validation receipt and no projection. Worse, the failure would have looked like a transient tooling problem rather than what it is — the still-outstanding defect 1 of six that BLOCKed repair-3 (BEN-044) — so the likely next move under "finish the task" pressure is to *fix the flags* and re-run, producing a chain that executes and is still wrong on the other three sub-parts of defect 1 plus defects 2–6. **So the gate's value here was not that it caught a bad candidate; it was that it stopped an agent from turning six known unrepaired defects into a plausible-looking artifact.** That is the argument for binding the token to a receipt rather than deleting the gate as advisory: an advisory gate that is honoured only by convention did, in this instance, do the entire job. Note also that a fix must not be "check the variable harder" — an agent that can set an env var can write a receipt file; bind it to the sha256 of a `standard-p4-verifier` receipt whose `verdict` is PASS **and** whose `code_rev` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`, or drop the variable and read that receipt directly. | **OPEN — gate is advisory in practice; treat as human checkpoint. Demonstrated load-bearing 2026-08-07: an autonomous run would have crossed it and broken a stage.** | `docs/orchestration/RUNBOOK-20260807-gbdt-closeout.md` §5; `nd-unfolding/run_p4_standard.sh:11,41`; `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` #22; `docs/orchestration/REPAIR4-DEFECT-STATUS-20260807.md` |

    44	## Resume-skip validates existence, not completeness (found 2026-07-17, 4D corrected uthrow)
    45	`[[ -s $OUT ]] && skip` resume guards (used across many sbatch launchers) treat any non-empty
    46	output as done. Producers that atomic-save per-unit into one file (e.g. `unified_throw_cov.py
    47	do_throws` per-throw saves) leave VALID-but-partial files when interrupted — the resume then
    48	permanently skips them. Bit us: comb4dCc 55971617 failed on 15/160 missing throws because slabs
    49	31,34-39 were partial leftovers of an interrupted multinode run; all 40 array tasks "COMPLETED".
    50	Caught only by the combine's `--expected-throws` manifest gate. Repair: partials moved to
    51	`uq_4d/corrected/uthrow_slabs_4d/partial_20260716_interrupted/`, regen 56025478 -> combine
    52	56025481 -> adopt 56025483. Fix pattern for future launchers: content-validated resume (open the
    53	file, check unit inventory) or write-to-temp + rename-on-complete. (BEN-023.)
    54	
    55	**FIXED REPO-WIDE 2026-08-01** (closes BEN-023 and audit J35 + J10, which are the same defect
    56	found independently in two subtrees). Completion is now an explicit record, not an inference from
    57	size: `lib/resume_guard.sh` provides `rg_skip_if_complete` / `rg_run` / `rg_publish`, which stamp a
    58	`${OUT}.done` marker **only after the producer exits 0** and bind it to the output's size+mtime, so
    59	a later truncation invalidates its own marker. An interrupted producer cannot leave one behind, so
    60	the resume re-runs. 85 guards across 84 shell files converted. The marker convention is deliberately
    61	the one `nd-unfolding/run_p4_unfold_std.sh` already used — that script was the in-repo precedent and
    62	is left alone, as is `run_p4_merge_audit_std.sh`; both already validate content.
    63	
    64	On the Python side (J10) `nd-unfolding/pet/atomic_write.py` carries the transaction —
    65	temp sibling → fsync → `os.replace` → marker last — and `train_fullevent_nominal.py:254` uses it
    66	instead of the bare `np.savez_compressed`, plus a no-clobber guard that refuses to replace an
    67	output already marked complete (`--allow-overwrite` opts in) and that fires *before* the eight
    68	GPU-hours. Gate-4 re-issued as
    69	`docs/orchestration/state/p3f-pet-gate4-launch-code-gate-20260801.json` (Step 2b; no physics
    70	re-run). `fullevent_dump_contract.py` was deliberately left byte-identical — it is frozen by the
    71	G2 **dump-provenance** receipt, not a code gate; see that receipt's `not_reissued_deliberately`.
    72	
    73	**Two traps in the fix itself.**
    74	1. **Nothing on disk has a marker.** The first resume after this lands re-runs everything.
    75	   Run `lib/backfill_completion_markers.sh --validator {root|npz} --glob '<pattern>'` over the live
    76	   output trees *before* resubmitting — RESTORE-2026-08-03 Step 0b. Read its FAIL list: those are
    77	   the partials the old guard was hiding.
    78	2. **`RESUME_ADOPT_LEGACY=1` is the old bug, opted into.** It adopts on a bare size check and warns
    79	   every time. Prefer a validator.
    80	
    81	Regression-pinned by `nd-unfolding/tests/test_resume_guard.py`, whose repo-wide scan fails if
    82	`[[ -s $OUT ]] && skip` reappears anywhere, and `nd-unfolding/tests/test_atomic_write.py`.

    84	## The engine's "Last val loss" prints the FIRST epoch, not the last
    85	
    86	`omnifold_nn/omnifold/omnifold.py:303` logs `hist.history['val_loss'][0]` under the label
    87	`Last val loss`. Index 0 is **epoch 1**. Anyone judging convergence from the training log is reading the
    88	first epoch of the fit.
    89	
    90	Found 2026-08-06 by a fresh-context review of the D2 powered-closure FAIL (job 56381674), and it had
    91	already done damage: two sessions independently proposed "the fit is optimization-limited, raise
    92	`epochs`" without opening the history pickles. The pickles refute it -- step-2 train loss moves 3.2e-5
    93	across 8 epochs in iteration 2, and that iteration's `val_loss` gets *worse* (0.829560 -> 0.829612, best
    94	at epoch 1). A fit with no remaining gradient signal, mislabelled as a fit starved of steps.
    95	
    96	Related, same file: `ModelCheckpoint(save_best_only=True)` (`:272-275`) writes **best-val** weights, while
    97	`reweight` uses the **last-epoch in-memory** model. On-disk checkpoints are therefore not bit-identical to
    98	what a run actually used -- calibrate before trusting an inference-only reproduction from them.
    99	
   100	Fixing the label touches `omnifold.py`, which is hash-bound by the Gate-4 launch-code gate, so it must
   101	ride a deliberate re-issue rather than a drive-by edit.
   102	
   103	Extended 2026-08-07: the plateau is a property of **all six** trainings of `56381674`, not just iteration
   104	2 (train loss moves 1.13e-3 across 8 epochs on the first, 3.0e-5 on the last; val argmin at {5,5,7,1,6,5}
   105	of 8). Two consequences for anyone reading these logs. `EarlyStopping(patience=10)` **cannot fire** at
   106	`epochs=8`, and Keras 2.15 restores best weights *only* inside its stop branch (`on_train_end` merely
   107	prints) -- so every run on this campaign has used last-epoch weights, and the `ModelCheckpoint` mismatch
   108	noted above is therefore the norm rather than an edge case. `ReduceLROnPlateau` is at `patience=1000`
   109	(`:263-265`) and `get_optimizer` returns a bare Adam at a flat LR (`:376-380`, `num_steps` accepted and
   110	unused), so no schedule ever engages either. Table and consequences:
   111	`docs/orchestration/FINDING-20260807-d2-underfitting-probe.md` §1.

   113	## The FPS extractor divides the cross section by a reco efficiency it must not divide by
   114	
   115	**RESOLVED 2026-08-06** (option A, authorized by Joseph; fix reviewed by an independent fresh-context
   116	session before commit). Left here rather than deleted: the *reason it survived* is the reusable part.
   117	
   118	**Severity, CORRECTED.** The first write-up of this entry said "2.36x on the integral and 398x in the
   119	lowest `p_parallel` bin". Both numbers were wrong and both were too small:
   120	
   121	* `2.36 = 1/<a>` is what you would get dividing the *aggregate* by the *global* acceptance. The code
   122	  divided **cell by cell**, so by Jensen the integral inflates far more:
   123	  `sum_b m_b/a_b / sum_b m_b = **122.6**` from the committed acceptance map, and **48-177x** per pT row
   124	  over the rows carrying >99% of the truth mass.
   125	* `398 = 1/0.00251` is the `p_parallel` **marginal slice** [0, 0.75], not a cell. The worst single
   126	  **cell** is `a_b = 0.0012397`, i.e. **807x**.
   127	
   128	Recomputed independently this turn from `products/pet/fullevent_fps/acceptance_map_fullevent_fps.json`.
   129	Legs 1-3 below were verified in source before the finding was relayed.
   130	
   131	1. `extract_fullevent_fps.py:390-404` `completeness_2d` computes
   132	   `c = sum_w(pass_truth & pass_reco) / sum_w(pass_truth)` -- **reco efficiency**. Its docstring says
   133	   "Verbatim `PETxsec5D._comp`".
   134	2. `xsec_nd.py:79` places it in the **denominator**: `denom = completeness * flux * n_nucleons * pot * vol`.
   135	3. `extract_fullevent_fps.py:431-434` histograms `(w_truth * push)` over **all** `pass_truth` rows,
   136	   including truth-only misses, whose `push` is the `nu_k` OmniFold step 2 assigns them
   137	   (`omnifold.py:218-220`). `counts` is therefore **already acceptance-corrected**, so dividing by
   138	   efficiency is a **double correction**.
   139	
   140	On this exact 285-cell grid the correct completeness is **identically 1**: the validated GBDT FPS unfolds
   141	carry `globalCompleteness = 1.0000000000000002` with all 266 nonzero `hCompletenessND_flat` bins at
   142	1.000000, and `unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:993-999` defines completeness as a **coverage** correction,
   143	not an efficiency. `PETxsec5D` only ever survived carrying an efficiency there because
   144	`pet_systematics_5d.py:127-141` overrides its own value with the GBDT one; the FPS port deliberately
   145	dropped that anchor (`extract_fullevent_fps.py:459-461`, "NONE -- no such anchor exists for this domain").
   146	**That comment is false** -- the anchor exists in this repo, on this grid, and it is the constant 1.
   147	
   148	**Two tests look like coverage and provide none:**
   149	
   150	- `tests/test_fullevent_extract.py:351-376` recomputes the formula by calling `ex.completeness_2d` **itself**
   151	  and asserts bit-equality (`rtol=0, atol=0`). It verifies the extractor calls the helpers it calls, and has
   152	  **zero power** over whether the quantity is the right physics. This is the self-agreement antipattern of
   153	  `AUDIT-FINDINGS-20260729-B.md` section 4.
   154	- `tests/test_fullevent_extract.py:331-342` **pins the reco-efficiency semantics as intended behaviour**, so
   155	  anyone repairing the double-correction must first break a test that reads as authoritative.
   156	
   157	**FIXED via (A): the division is gone.** Joseph authorized (A) on 2026-08-06. The argument recorded in
   158	the extractor is now **structural rather than empirical**: `extract_cross_section_nd`'s `completeness`
   159	argument means *coverage of the truth denominator by the OmniFold input*
   160	(`unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:992-999` builds it as `of_in/denom_nd`), and this extractor has no
   161	separate truth denominator -- the declared fiducial domain **is** `pass_truth` -- so coverage is **1 by
   162	construction**. The GBDT `globalCompleteness = 1.0000000000000002` is corroboration, not the reason;
   163	leading with the measurement is what invites a future re-anchoring. Option (B) (mask `counts` to
   164	`pass_truth & pass_reco`) was rejected: it would delete the FPS extension the campaign exists to add.
   165	
   166	`comp` keeps one role, **as a reporting mask only**. It subsumes `denom > 0` by construction, so the
   167	reported domain is set entirely by the reco efficiency; this **preserves** the pre-fix domain, since
   168	`comp == 0` already forced those cells to 0. It is a **floor**, not the acceptance-supported vs
   169	model-dependent tiering decision, which remains open at `docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md:430-438` and covers far more
   170	truth mass (25.93% below `a_b < 0.01`) than this mask's 4 cells (4.6e-7 of truth mass).
   171	
   172	Coverage = 1 is now **guarded, not assumed**: `assert_truth_denominator_coverage` fails closed, mirroring
   173	`unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:747-752`, which raises rather than assuming its analogue.
   174	
   175	**Step 4b is unblocked.** Step 4 was never affected.
   176	
   177	## The same construction exists in `pointcloud_projection.py`, off the gated path
   178	
   179	`nd-unfolding/pet/pointcloud_projection.py:236-241` has the identical shape -- `counts` over
   180	`pass_truth`, `comp = ofin/denom`, passed as the divisor. It is **not** on the gated publication product
   181	path, so it is recorded rather than fixed, so that it is not rediscovered as a new finding. Anything
   182	promoting that path to a product must settle it first.
   183	
   184	## The closure driver persists no inference contract
   185	
   186	`closure_powered_truth_reweight.py:287` saves only `dump_rows_a/b`, `weights_push`, `mc_indices`.
   187	Architecture comes from `meta` (`:261-263`) and the input normalization is derived inside
   188	`build_fullevent_loaders` at run time, so **there is no stored normalization to assert against** when
   189	reproducing a run by inference. The nominal driver stores its norms; the closure driver does not. Any
   190	inference-only reproduction must reproduce the same row population (`dump_rows_b` makes that possible) and
   191	must treat the spectrum reproduction as its only falsification handle.

   193	## The PET covariance summaries carry no estimator stamp — the fact lives only in the launcher
   194	
   195	`products/pet/bkgsub/pet_cstat_bkgsub_5d.summary.json` and its siblings record `n_replicas`,
   196	`replica_ids`, `n_reported_bins`, the sqrt-trace and per-bin ratios — and **nothing about the estimator
   197	that produced them**: no `niter`, no schema/feature set, no commit, no job id. Their producers
   198	(`pet/combine_cstat_bkgsub.py`, `pet/assemble_ctotal_bkgsub.py`) do not record it either, because they
   199	combine replica outputs and never see the training config.
   200	
   201	**Correction, 2026-08-06:** an earlier version of this entry said the fact "was never written down."
   202	That is wrong, and wrong in the direction that matters. `pet/sbatch_pet_nominal_bkgsub.sh:42` pins
   203	`NITER="${PET_NITER:-2}"`, its header at `:29` states `iters = 2` in as many words, and `:14` carries
   204	the banner **"QUARANTINED RECOIL-ONLY CROSS-CHECK LAUNCHER — NOT a publication path"**, with `:15-17`
   205	naming the recoil loader and the bkgsub purity target and noting that "C_stat, C_ml, and systematic
   206	blocks all reference THIS nominal." So the provenance is recorded — just not in the artifact a reader
   207	of the covariance would open.
   208	
   209	That makes the classification **stronger**, not weaker. These components are disqualified from the
   210	`niter=3` budget by three *positive* facts, not by an absence: they were built at **`niter=2`**, on a
   211	path the repo itself labels **non-publication**, over a **10550-bin recoil domain** (against 10694 for
   212	the 5D lane re-rolled in `uq_5d/rescaled_20260806/j28_reroll_20260806.json`). This satisfies
   213	`PLAN-20260806-niter3-budget-and-J28-reroll.md` rule 5, which demands a stated reason rather than the
   214	absence of a reason to doubt.
   215	
   216	The debt that remains is the **stamp**, and it is real: nothing in the artifact chain would have told a
   217	future reader any of the above, and the whole `bkgsub` budget — C_syst, C_retrain, C_stat, C_ml,
   218	C_lateral and the assembled C_total — hangs off that one quarantined nominal.
   219	
   220	**Fix forward:** any new covariance component must stamp the estimator config it was computed under
   221	(at minimum `niter`, schema/feature-set identifier, and the producing commit) into its own summary,
   222	the way `train_fullevent_nominal.py` stamps `seed_policy` into its weights artifact. A covariance
   223	without that stamp is unclassifiable from the artifact the moment the estimator moves, and the
   224	estimator has now moved twice (full-event schema 2026-08-01, `niter` 2026-08-06).

   226	## `step1_class_ratio` in the nominal artifact is a stored TARGET, not an achieved measurement
   227	
   228	Found 2026-08-07 by making the mistake. Investigating the nominal's fold-forward failure I read
   229	`pet_fullevent_nominal_weights.npz`'s `step1_class_ratio = 1.1240802949941018`, saw it equal Gate-2's R
   230	exactly, and concluded *"not the classic step-1 defect — that signature is the class ratio forced to 1, ours
   231	is exactly R."* **That inference is invalid.** `train_fullevent_nominal.py:464` sets
   232	`class_ratio = target_meta.get("step1_class_ratio")` — from the loader's target metadata — and stores it
   233	verbatim at `:505`. `fullevent_fps_dataloader.step1_class_ratio_from_dump` derives R from the dump's data/MC
   234	yields. So the field is **the target R, re-stored**; it can never disagree with R and therefore carries **zero
   235	information** about what step 1 achieved. Agreement is tautological.
   236	
   237	The trap is the name. A field called `step1_class_ratio` sitting beside genuine measurements
   238	(`cap_saturation_frac`, `fold_forward_sum_w_push_reco`) reads as "the class ratio step 1 produced". It is a
   239	copy of the input. **Consequence:** the step-1 under-achievement hypothesis is *not* ruled out for the
   240	2026-08-07 nominal, and it is now the leading candidate — the historical defect drives the effective ratio
   241	toward 1, and a folded-forward ratio of 0.7465 against a required 1.1241 is the right direction for it.
   242	
   243	**Fix forward, two parts.** (1) Rename or re-document the stored field so it cannot be read as an outcome —
   244	`step1_class_ratio_target` would have prevented this. (2) If an achieved value is wanted, it has to be
   245	*measured*: run inference with the saved `w_nominal/*_step1.weights.h5` and compare the classifier's
   246	reco-space mean against R. Nothing currently stored supports that comparison.

    44	## Resume-skip validates existence, not completeness (found 2026-07-17, 4D corrected uthrow)
    45	`[[ -s $OUT ]] && skip` resume guards (used across many sbatch launchers) treat any non-empty
    46	output as done. Producers that atomic-save per-unit into one file (e.g. `unified_throw_cov.py
    47	do_throws` per-throw saves) leave VALID-but-partial files when interrupted — the resume then
    48	permanently skips them. Bit us: comb4dCc 55971617 failed on 15/160 missing throws because slabs
    49	31,34-39 were partial leftovers of an interrupted multinode run; all 40 array tasks "COMPLETED".
    50	Caught only by the combine's `--expected-throws` manifest gate. Repair: partials moved to
    51	`uq_4d/corrected/uthrow_slabs_4d/partial_20260716_interrupted/`, regen 56025478 -> combine
    52	56025481 -> adopt 56025483. Fix pattern for future launchers: content-validated resume (open the
    53	file, check unit inventory) or write-to-temp + rename-on-complete. (BEN-023.)
    54	
    55	**FIXED REPO-WIDE 2026-08-01** (closes BEN-023 and audit J35 + J10, which are the same defect
    56	found independently in two subtrees). Completion is now an explicit record, not an inference from
    57	size: `lib/resume_guard.sh` provides `rg_skip_if_complete` / `rg_run` / `rg_publish`, which stamp a
    58	`${OUT}.done` marker **only after the producer exits 0** and bind it to the output's size+mtime, so
    59	a later truncation invalidates its own marker. An interrupted producer cannot leave one behind, so
    60	the resume re-runs. 85 guards across 84 shell files converted. The marker convention is deliberately
    61	the one `nd-unfolding/run_p4_unfold_std.sh` already used — that script was the in-repo precedent and
    62	is left alone, as is `run_p4_merge_audit_std.sh`; both already validate content.
    63	
    64	On the Python side (J10) `nd-unfolding/pet/atomic_write.py` carries the transaction —
    65	temp sibling → fsync → `os.replace` → marker last — and `train_fullevent_nominal.py:254` uses it
    66	instead of the bare `np.savez_compressed`, plus a no-clobber guard that refuses to replace an
    67	output already marked complete (`--allow-overwrite` opts in) and that fires *before* the eight
    68	GPU-hours. Gate-4 re-issued as
    69	`docs/orchestration/state/p3f-pet-gate4-launch-code-gate-20260801.json` (Step 2b; no physics
    70	re-run). `fullevent_dump_contract.py` was deliberately left byte-identical — it is frozen by the
    71	G2 **dump-provenance** receipt, not a code gate; see that receipt's `not_reissued_deliberately`.
    72	
    73	**Two traps in the fix itself.**
    74	1. **Nothing on disk has a marker.** The first resume after this lands re-runs everything.
    75	   Run `lib/backfill_completion_markers.sh --validator {root|npz} --glob '<pattern>'` over the live
    76	   output trees *before* resubmitting — RESTORE-2026-08-03 Step 0b. Read its FAIL list: those are
    77	   the partials the old guard was hiding.
    78	2. **`RESUME_ADOPT_LEGACY=1` is the old bug, opted into.** It adopts on a bare size check and warns
    79	   every time. Prefer a validator.
    80	
    81	Regression-pinned by `nd-unfolding/tests/test_resume_guard.py`, whose repo-wide scan fails if
    82	`[[ -s $OUT ]] && skip` reappears anywhere, and `nd-unfolding/tests/test_atomic_write.py`.

    84	## The engine's "Last val loss" prints the FIRST epoch, not the last
    85	
    86	`omnifold_nn/omnifold/omnifold.py:303` logs `hist.history['val_loss'][0]` under the label
    87	`Last val loss`. Index 0 is **epoch 1**. Anyone judging convergence from the training log is reading the
    88	first epoch of the fit.
    89	
    90	Found 2026-08-06 by a fresh-context review of the D2 powered-closure FAIL (job 56381674), and it had
    91	already done damage: two sessions independently proposed "the fit is optimization-limited, raise
    92	`epochs`" without opening the history pickles. The pickles refute it -- step-2 train loss moves 3.2e-5
    93	across 8 epochs in iteration 2, and that iteration's `val_loss` gets *worse* (0.829560 -> 0.829612, best
    94	at epoch 1). A fit with no remaining gradient signal, mislabelled as a fit starved of steps.
    95	
    96	Related, same file: `ModelCheckpoint(save_best_only=True)` (`:272-275`) writes **best-val** weights, while
    97	`reweight` uses the **last-epoch in-memory** model. On-disk checkpoints are therefore not bit-identical to
    98	what a run actually used -- calibrate before trusting an inference-only reproduction from them.
    99	
   100	Fixing the label touches `omnifold.py`, which is hash-bound by the Gate-4 launch-code gate, so it must
   101	ride a deliberate re-issue rather than a drive-by edit.
   102

   104	2 (train loss moves 1.13e-3 across 8 epochs on the first, 3.0e-5 on the last; val argmin at {5,5,7,1,6,5}
   105	of 8). Two consequences for anyone reading these logs. `EarlyStopping(patience=10)` **cannot fire** at
   106	`epochs=8`, and Keras 2.15 restores best weights *only* inside its stop branch (`on_train_end` merely
   107	prints) -- so every run on this campaign has used last-epoch weights, and the `ModelCheckpoint` mismatch

   110	unused), so no schedule ever engages either. Table and consequences:

   113	## The FPS extractor divides the cross section by a reco efficiency it must not divide by
   114	
   115	**RESOLVED 2026-08-06** (option A, authorized by Joseph; fix reviewed by an independent fresh-context
   116	session before commit). Left here rather than deleted: the *reason it survived* is the reusable part.
   117	
   118	**Severity, CORRECTED.** The first write-up of this entry said "2.36x on the integral and 398x in the
   119	lowest `p_parallel` bin". Both numbers were wrong and both were too small:
   120	
   121	* `2.36 = 1/<a>` is what you would get dividing the *aggregate* by the *global* acceptance. The code
   122	  divided **cell by cell**, so by Jensen the integral inflates far more:
   123	  `sum_b m_b/a_b / sum_b m_b = **122.6**` from the committed acceptance map, and **48-177x** per pT row
   124	  over the rows carrying >99% of the truth mass.
   125	* `398 = 1/0.00251` is the `p_parallel` **marginal slice** [0, 0.75], not a cell. The worst single
   126	  **cell** is `a_b = 0.0012397`, i.e. **807x**.
   127	
   128	Recomputed independently this turn from `products/pet/fullevent_fps/acceptance_map_fullevent_fps.json`.
   129	Legs 1-3 below were verified in source before the finding was relayed.
   130	
   131	1. `extract_fullevent_fps.py:390-404` `completeness_2d` computes
   132	   `c = sum_w(pass_truth & pass_reco) / sum_w(pass_truth)` -- **reco efficiency**. Its docstring says
   133	   "Verbatim `PETxsec5D._comp`".
   134	2. `xsec_nd.py:79` places it in the **denominator**: `denom = completeness * flux * n_nucleons * pot * vol`.
   135	3. `extract_fullevent_fps.py:431-434` histograms `(w_truth * push)` over **all** `pass_truth` rows,
   136	   including truth-only misses, whose `push` is the `nu_k` OmniFold step 2 assigns them
   137	   (`omnifold.py:218-220`). `counts` is therefore **already acceptance-corrected**, so dividing by
   138	   efficiency is a **double correction**.
   139	
   140	On this exact 285-cell grid the correct completeness is **identically 1**: the validated GBDT FPS unfolds
   141	carry `globalCompleteness = 1.0000000000000002` with all 266 nonzero `hCompletenessND_flat` bins at
   142	1.000000, and `unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:993-999` defines completeness as a **coverage** correction,
   143	not an efficiency. `PETxsec5D` only ever survived carrying an efficiency there because
   144	`pet_systematics_5d.py:127-141` overrides its own value with the GBDT one; the FPS port deliberately
   145	dropped that anchor (`extract_fullevent_fps.py:459-461`, "NONE -- no such anchor exists for this domain").
   146	**That comment is false** -- the anchor exists in this repo, on this grid, and it is the constant 1.
   147	
   148	**Two tests look like coverage and provide none:**
   149	
   150	- `tests/test_fullevent_extract.py:351-376` recomputes the formula by calling `ex.completeness_2d` **itself**
   151	  and asserts bit-equality (`rtol=0, atol=0`). It verifies the extractor calls the helpers it calls, and has
   152	  **zero power** over whether the quantity is the right physics. This is the self-agreement antipattern of
   153	  `AUDIT-FINDINGS-20260729-B.md` section 4.
   154	- `tests/test_fullevent_extract.py:331-342` **pins the reco-efficiency semantics as intended behaviour**, so
   155	  anyone repairing the double-correction must first break a test that reads as authoritative.
   156	
   157	**FIXED via (A): the division is gone.** Joseph authorized (A) on 2026-08-06. The argument recorded in
   158	the extractor is now **structural rather than empirical**: `extract_cross_section_nd`'s `completeness`
   159	argument means *coverage of the truth denominator by the OmniFold input*
   160	(`unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py:992-999` builds it as `of_in/denom_nd`), and this extractor has no
   161	separate truth denominator -- the declared fiducial domain **is** `pass_truth` -- so coverage is **1 by
   162	construction**. The GBDT `globalCompleteness = 1.0000000000000002` is corroboration, not the reason;
   163	leading with the measurement is what invites a future re-anchoring. Option (B) (mask `counts` to
   164	`pass_truth & pass_reco`) was rejected: it would delete the FPS extension the campaign exists to add.
   165	
   166	`comp` keeps one role, **as a reporting mask only**. It subsumes `denom > 0` by construction, so the
   167	reported domain is set entirely by the reco efficiency; this **preserves** the pre-fix domain, since
   168	`comp == 0` already forced those cells to 0. It is a **floor**, not the acceptance-supported vs
   169	model-dependent tiering decision, which remains open at `docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md:430-438` and covers far more
   170	truth mass (25.93% below `a_b < 0.01`) than this mask's 4 cells (4.6e-7 of truth mass).
   171	
   172	Coverage = 1 is now **guarded, not assumed**: `assert_truth_denominator_coverage` fails closed, mirroring

   239	copy of the input. **Consequence:** the step-1 under-achievement hypothesis is *not* ruled out for the
   240	2026-08-07 nominal, and it is now the leading candidate — the historical defect drives the effective ratio

   282	## J28's scope misses a sixth site: `eavailW_covariance.py` divides every flux universe by the CV flux
   283	
   284	The J28 fix commit `081ae4a` touches **12 files and `eavailW_covariance.py` is not among them**, and
   285	neither `AUDIT-FINDINGS-20260731.md` nor this file scopes it into J28's blast radius. But it carries
   286	the same defect by the same mechanism:
   287	
   288	- `:104` loads `flux_bins` **once**, from the CV histogram `pTmu_reweightedflux_integrated`;
   289	- `:232` passes that same CV array into `extract_cross_section_nd` on **every** call, with no
   290	  per-universe override — contrast a fixed site, `unified_throw_cov_5d.py:67`, which threads
   291	  `d["flux"] if flux is None else flux` precisely so a universe can supply its own `Φu`;
   292	- `:259 def _y_band(sig_u, td_u)` takes weight arrays only — there is no flux parameter to thread;
   293	- `:274-276` runs **all 100 PPFX flux universes** through `_y_band` and forms
   294	  `C_flux = mat_covariance(fX)`, added into `C_syst` at `:277`.
   295	
   296	So every flux universe is divided by `Φ_CV` instead of its own `Φu`, which **removes the normalization
   297	spread the flux universes exist to carry** and therefore *understates* `C_flux`. Direction is fixed by
   298	the same identity the re-roll used; magnitude is not, because this is a **code read and has not been
   299	run** — do not quote a number for it. For scale only, the analogous correction in the 5D lane raised
   300	`sqrt_tr_flux_block` by 316.83%.
   301	
   302	Nothing quoted today is wrong: `values.tex:53-54` records the (E_avail,W) significances as removed
   303	2026-07-12, and `sec_eavailw.tex:136-138` states compatibility "is not evaluated without the corrected
   304	projected covariance." But that corrected covariance **is** a stated deliverable, and it could not be
   305	built from this script as it stood. Found 2026-08-06 by a fresh-context review of the Step 2
   306	classification and confirmed independently at the mechanism level.
   307	
   308	**CODE FIXED 2026-08-06, NO NUMBER PRODUCED — the same footing 081ae4a had for the first five sites**
   309	("the code fix is committed, fail-closed, and mutation-tested … no corrected number exists yet").
   310	`xsec_ew` and `_y_band` now take a `flux` override, and the flux loop resolves a per-universe table via
   311	`flux_universe.resolve_flux_ratio_table` — reusing the helper 081ae4a already shipped rather than
   312	inventing a mechanism. `flux=None` still means the CV flux, which is **correct** for the CV and for
   313	every knob band (a knob does not move the flux integral) and wrong only for a flux universe; same
   314	`d["flux"] if flux is None else flux` shape as `unified_throw_cov_5d.py:67`.
   315

   138	_PURITY_SIGNATURE = "[INFO] measured training:"

   141	def classify_log_bkg_mode(text):
   142	    """Return (mode, reason) for one unfold log. mode is a member of KNOWN_BKG_MODES, or
   143	    None when the log cannot decide -- which callers must treat as UNPROVABLE, not as
   144	    'probably fine'."""
   145	    announced = None
   146	    for line in text.splitlines():
   147	        i = line.find(_BKG_MODE_ANNOUNCE)
   148	        if i >= 0:
   149	            tail = line[i + len(_BKG_MODE_ANNOUNCE):]
   150	            tok = tail.split(":", 1)[0].strip()
   151	            if tok in KNOWN_BKG_MODES:
   152	                if announced is not None and announced != tok:
   153	                    return None, f"log announces conflicting modes {announced!r} and {tok!r}"
   154	                announced = tok
   155	            else:
   156	                return None, f"log announces unrecognized bkg-mode {tok!r}"
   157	    if announced is not None:
   158	        if announced == "purity":
   159	            # the purity branch never announces; an announcement claiming purity means the
   160	            # log did not come from this driver's known print set.
   161	            return None, "log announces bkg-mode=purity, which this driver's purity branch never prints"
   162	        return announced, f"driver announced bkg-mode={announced}"
   163	    if _PURITY_SIGNATURE in text:
   164	        return "purity", ("no bkg-mode announcement + build_measured_training_nd signature "
   165	                          "present => purity branch (the silent branch)")
   166	    return None, ("no bkg-mode announcement and no measured-training signature; the run may "
   167	                  "have been non-verbose, so the branch is unprovable from this log")

   201	def require_candidate_path(path):
   202	    """Positive allowlist + negative denylist: a candidate MUST live under the
   203	    candidate subdir and MUST NOT match any adopted/protected token. Prevents both
   204	    the round-2 self-rejection (candidate name containing '_final') and any write
   205	    onto an adopted/central path."""
   206	    # repair-5 (defect 4a). History: this was first a bare substring test, then a
   207	    # normpath component match -- and the verifier defeated the second one too, because a
   208	    # component match succeeds ANYWHERE the sequence appears, so
   209	    # `/evil/active_universe_5d/standard/candidate/out.root` passed, and normpath does not
   210	    # resolve symlinks. Containment must be RESOLVED and anchored to this repository:
   211	    # realpath both sides, then require commonpath(candidate_root, target) == candidate_root.
   212	    cand_root = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(ND_ROOT, CANDIDATE_SUBDIR))
   213	    # Callers pass repo-relative ("nd-unfolding/active_universe_5d/...") or ND-relative
   214	    # ("active_universe_5d/...") paths depending on where they cd to, so resolve a relative
   215	    # path against BOTH known roots and accept it if either lands inside. An absolute path is
   216	    # taken as given. Resolution is realpath, so symlinks cannot smuggle a target out.
   217	    if os.path.isabs(path):
   218	        cands = [path]
   219	    else:
   220	        cands = [os.path.join(ND_ROOT, path), os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, path)]
   221	    resolved, inside = None, False
   222	    for c in cands:
   223	        t = os.path.realpath(c)
   224	        if resolved is None:
   225	            resolved = t
   226	        try:
   227	            if os.path.commonpath([cand_root, t]) == cand_root and t != cand_root:
   228	                resolved, inside = t, True
   229	                break
   230	        except ValueError:                 # different drives / unrelated roots
   231	            continue
   232	    require(inside,
   233	            f"candidate must resolve inside {cand_root} (got {path} -> {resolved})")
   234	    for t in _ADOPTED_TOKENS:
   235	        require(t not in path, f"refusing candidate onto adopted/protected path (token {t!r})")
   236	    return True

   239	def prove_identity(A, B, rtol, label):
   240	    """Fail-closed max-relative-difference identity gate (no subtraction hidden)."""
   241	    A = np.asarray(A, dtype=float); B = np.asarray(B, dtype=float)
   242	    require(A.shape == B.shape, f"{label}: shape {A.shape} != {B.shape}")
   243	    denom = max(1e-300, float(np.max(np.abs(A))))
   244	    err = float(np.max(np.abs(A - B)) / denom)
   245	    require(err <= rtol, f"{label}: identity broken (rel {err:.2e} > {rtol:.0e})")
   246	    return err

   249	def edges_bin_volume_hash(edges):
   250	    """Hash the ordered 5-axis edge arrays + the C-order per-bin volume vector."""
   251	    import numpy as _np
   252	    parts = []
   253	    for e in edges:
   254	        a = _np.asarray(e, dtype=float); require(a.ndim == 1 and a.size >= 2, "bad edge array")
   255	        parts.append(a.tobytes())
   256	    edge_hash = hashlib.sha256(b"|".join(parts)).hexdigest()
   257	    widths = [(_np.asarray(e, float)[1:] - _np.asarray(e, float)[:-1]) for e in edges]
   258	    vol = widths[0]
   259	    for w in widths[1:]:
   260	        vol = _np.multiply.outer(vol, w).ravel()   # C-order product of bin widths
   261	    vol_hash = hashlib.sha256(vol.astype(float).tobytes() + b"|C").hexdigest()
   262	    return {"edge_hash": edge_hash, "bin_volume_hash": vol_hash, "n_bins": int(vol.size)}

   265	def validate_orchestrator_merged_receipt(recdir, live_stat):
   266	    """Consume the owner-neutral merged-hash receipt: require COMPLETE + the four
   267	    files, recompute live size/integer-mtime vs the inventory, and return the
   268	    committed hash-list digest bound into our manifest. live_stat: dict path->(size,mtime)."""
   269	    import os as _os
   270	    for f in ("COMPLETE", "summary.tsv", "validation.tsv", "standard.sha256", "standard.inventory.tsv"):
   271	        require(_os.path.exists(_os.path.join(recdir, f)), f"orchestrator receipt missing {f}")
   272	    sha_lines = [l for l in open(_os.path.join(recdir, "standard.sha256")).read().splitlines() if l.strip()]
   273	    require(len(sha_lines) == N_ENDPOINTS, f"receipt standard.sha256 has {len(sha_lines)} != 10 lines")
   274	    merged = {}
   275	    for l in sha_lines:
   276	        h, p = l.split(None, 1); merged[p.strip()] = h
   277	    # recompute live size + integer mtime against the committed inventory
   278	    inv = {}
   279	    for l in open(_os.path.join(recdir, "standard.inventory.tsv")).read().splitlines():
   280	        if not l.strip() or l.startswith("#"):
   281	            continue
   282	        cols = l.split("\t")
   283	        if len(cols) >= 3:                       # orchestrator format: size<TAB>mtime<TAB>path
   284	            inv[cols[2]] = (int(cols[0]), int(float(cols[1])))
   285	    for p, (sz, mt) in inv.items():
   286	        require(p in live_stat, f"inventory path not live: {p}")
   287	        lsz, lmt = live_stat[p]
   288	        require(lsz == sz and int(lmt) == mt, f"live size/mtime drift for {p}")
   289	    digest = hashlib.sha256("\n".join(sorted(f"{merged[p]}  {p}" for p in merged)).encode()).hexdigest()
   290	    return {"merged_sha256": merged, "hash_list_digest": digest, "n": len(merged)}

   314	def validate_endpoint_receipt(rec, *, tag, root_sha256, merged_sha256,
   315	                              central5d_sha256, config_hash, bkg_mode,
   316	                              code_rev, unfold_blob):
   317	    """Fail closed unless the receipt is complete AND every recorded identity matches the
   318	    live/committed one. Returns True, or raises P4GateError naming the first mismatch.
   319	
   320	    REPAIR-5 (defect 2). The previous version required `code_rev` to be a NON-EMPTY STRING and
   321	    compared it to nothing, and the receipt recorded no source identity at all -- so an
   322	    endpoint produced under a changed unfold driver was still skipped. That is the third
   323	    instance in this chain of "assert presence, never compare": the first is the
   324	    `P4_VERIFIER_PASS` non-emptiness gate (KNOWN_ISSUES #21), the second is the `identities`
   325	    block whose members were literal `True`. Presence is not evidence; both `code_rev` and the
   326	    producing driver's committed blob are now COMPARED."""
   327	    require(isinstance(rec, dict) and rec, f"receipt for {tag} is not a JSON object")
   328	    missing = [k for k in RECEIPT_REQUIRED_KEYS if k not in rec]
   329	    require(not missing, f"receipt {tag} missing required keys {missing} (incomplete legacy format)")
   330	    require(rec["mode"] in RECEIPT_MODES, f"receipt {tag} unknown mode {rec['mode']!r}")
   331	    require(rec["tag"] == tag, f"receipt tag {rec['tag']!r} != {tag!r} (receipt/ROOT pair mismatch)")
   332	    require(rec["root_sha256"] == root_sha256,
   333	            f"receipt {tag} root_sha256 drift: recorded {rec['root_sha256']} vs live {root_sha256}")
   334	    require(rec["merged_sha256"] == merged_sha256,
   335	            f"receipt {tag} merged_sha256 drift vs the orchestrator receipt")
   336	    require(rec["central5d_sha256"] == central5d_sha256,
   337	            f"receipt {tag} central5d_sha256 drift (the central moved under this endpoint)")
   338	    require(rec["config_hash"] == config_hash,
   339	            f"receipt {tag} config_hash drift: produced under a different unfold configuration")
   340	    require(rec["bkg_mode"] == bkg_mode,
   341	            f"receipt {tag} bkg_mode {rec['bkg_mode']!r} != declared {bkg_mode!r}")
   342	    # D2: compared, not merely present.
   343	    require(isinstance(rec["code_rev"], str) and rec["code_rev"],
   344	            f"receipt {tag} has no code_rev")
   345	    require(isinstance(code_rev, str) and code_rev,
   346	            f"cannot validate receipt {tag}: no live code_rev to compare against")

   372	def matrix_content_hash(M):
   373	    """Deterministic digest of a matrix's CONTENTS (repair-4, defect 5d).
   374	
   375	    The projection receipt recorded only `M_shape`, which two different projectors of the same
   376	    dimensions share. Hashes C-contiguous float64 bytes plus the shape, so a changed weight is
   377	    caught and a transposed/reshaped M cannot collide with the original."""
   378	    A = np.ascontiguousarray(np.asarray(M, dtype=np.float64))
   379	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   380	    h.update(repr(A.shape).encode()); h.update(b"|C|f8|"); h.update(A.tobytes())
   381	    return h.hexdigest()

   384	def check_full_total_identity(Ccomb, Csyst, Cstat, Cml, rtol=1e-9):
   385	    """PROVE C_combined = C_syst + C_stat + C_ML by comparing the residual to the actual
   386	    stat and ML blocks. Returns the measured max-relative error.
   387	
   388	    REPAIR-5 (defect 4b / 6). Repair-4 checked only that `C_combined - C_syst` was symmetric
   389	    PSD and called that the full-total identity, in a gate name, a receipt field and a test
   390	    name. PSD is NECESSARY but nowhere near SUFFICIENT: every covariance-shaped residual passes
   391	    it, including one built from the wrong stat block, a doubled ML block, or a residual that
   392	    simply is not stat+ML at all. Naming a weak check after a strong claim is the same
   393	    "strong name over weak check" pattern as the test that passed because argparse rejected an
   394	    argument before the guard it named ever ran (verifier defect 6b). This compares."""
   395	    resid = np.asarray(Ccomb, float) - np.asarray(Csyst, float)
   396	    expect = np.asarray(Cstat, float) + np.asarray(Cml, float)
   397	    require(resid.shape == expect.shape,
   398	            f"full-total identity: residual {resid.shape} != stat+ML {expect.shape}")
   399	    # PSD of the residual is retained as a SEPARATE, weaker sanity check -- not as the identity.
   400	    check_symmetric_psd(resid)
   401	    return prove_identity(resid, expect, rtol, "C_combined - C_syst == C_stat + C_ML")

   434	def sha256_file(path, _bufsz=1 << 20):
   435	    """Durable file digest (login-computable; no ROOT)."""
   436	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   437	    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
   438	        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(_bufsz), b""):
   439	            h.update(chunk)
   440	    return h.hexdigest()

   521	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- covariance gates
   522	def check_symmetric_psd(C, rtol_sym=1e-9, psd_atol_ratio=1e-12):
   523	    C = np.asarray(C, dtype=float)
   524	    require(C.ndim == 2 and C.shape[0] == C.shape[1], "covariance must be square 2-D")
   525	    require(np.all(np.isfinite(C)), "covariance has non-finite entries")
   526	    denom = max(1e-300, np.max(np.abs(C)))
   527	    asym = np.max(np.abs(C - C.T)) / denom
   528	    require(asym <= rtol_sym, f"covariance not symmetric (rel {asym:.2e})")
   529	    ev = np.linalg.eigvalsh(0.5 * (C + C.T))
   530	    require(ev[0] >= -psd_atol_ratio * abs(ev[-1]),
   531	            f"covariance not PSD (min/max eig {ev[0]/max(1e-300,abs(ev[-1])):.2e})")
   532	    d = np.diag(C)
   533	    require(np.all(np.isfinite(d)) and np.all(d >= -1e-30), "non-finite/negative diagonal")
   534	    return {"rel_asymmetry": float(asym), "min_eig": float(ev[0]), "max_eig": float(ev[-1])}
   535

   557	def check_component_sum(total, band_covs, rtol=1e-9):
   558	    """total must equal the EXACT sum of the 5 per-band component covariances."""

   573	    """Complete support comparison: both present, same shape/mask/order. Returns
   574	    sqrt-trace ratio (active/support). Fail-closed if the support block is absent."""
   575	    require(active_cov is not None, "active lateral block missing")

   578	    require(A.shape == S.shape, f"active/support shape mismatch {A.shape} vs {S.shape}")
   579	    sta = float(np.sqrt(max(0.0, np.trace(A)))); sts = float(np.sqrt(max(0.0, np.trace(S))))
   580	    require(sts > 0, "support block has zero trace")
   581	    return {"sqrt_tr_active": sta, "sqrt_tr_support": sts, "ratio": sta / sts}

   584	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- deterministic projection map
   585	def build_projection_M(edges, drop_axis, mask_high, mask_low):
   586	    """Deterministic 5D->4D map by WIDTH-WEIGHTED marginalization of one axis.
   587	    edges: ordered per-axis edge arrays (pt,pz,eavail,q3,W). drop_axis: axis index to
   588	    marginalize (W=4). mask_high/mask_low: reported-bin bool masks over the full high/low
   589	    grids (C-order). Returns dense M (n_low_reported x n_high_reported) with
   590	    M[a,b] = width_drop[k] when high bin b decomposes to low bin a + dropped index k.
   591	    density convention: x_low = M @ x_high, C_low = M C_high M^T."""
   592	    nb = [np.asarray(e).size - 1 for e in edges]
   593	    require(len(nb) == 5, "expected 5 axes")
   594	    total_high = int(np.prod(nb))
   595	    require(int(np.asarray(mask_high).size) == total_high, "mask_high size != high grid")
   596	    wdrop = np.asarray(edges[drop_axis], float)[1:] - np.asarray(edges[drop_axis], float)[:-1]
   597	    nb_low = [n for i, n in enumerate(nb) if i != drop_axis]
   598	    total_low = int(np.prod(nb_low))
   599	    require(int(np.asarray(mask_low).size) == total_low, "mask_low size != low grid")
   600	    strides_h = np.array([int(np.prod(nb[i + 1:])) for i in range(5)])          # C-order strides
   601	    strides_l = np.array([int(np.prod(nb_low[i + 1:])) for i in range(4)])
   602	    mh = np.nonzero(np.asarray(mask_high).astype(bool))[0]
   603	    ml = np.nonzero(np.asarray(mask_low).astype(bool))[0]
   604	    low_pos = {int(g): r for r, g in enumerate(ml)}                              # low global -> reported row
   605	    M = np.zeros((ml.size, mh.size), dtype=float)
   606	    for col, g in enumerate(mh):
   607	        midx = [(g // strides_h[i]) % nb[i] for i in range(5)]                   # 5D multi-index
   608	        k = midx[drop_axis]
   609	        low_multi = [midx[i] for i in range(5) if i != drop_axis]
   610	        glow = int(np.dot(low_multi, strides_l))
   611	        row = low_pos.get(glow)
   612	        require(row is not None, f"high reported bin {g} maps to non-reported low bin {glow}")
   613	        M[row, col] = wdrop[k]
   614	    return M
   615

   617	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- projection gates
   618	def project(C_high, M):
   619	    """5D->4D (or any) projection C_low = M C_high M^T (preserves density/order)."""
   620	    C_high = np.asarray(C_high, dtype=float); M = np.asarray(M, dtype=float)
   621	    require(M.shape[1] == C_high.shape[0], f"M cols {M.shape[1]} != C dim {C_high.shape[0]}")
   622	    return M @ C_high @ M.T
   623	
   624	
   625	def check_projection_nonmutation(C_high, M, x_high, x_low_frozen, rtol_central=3e-2):
   626	    """Enforce projected covariance validity AND central non-mutation:
   627	    C_low = M C_high M^T is symmetric/PSD, and M @ x_high reproduces the frozen
   628	    lower-dim central within tolerance (the projection must not mutate the central)."""
   629	    C_low = project(C_high, M)
   630	    stats = check_symmetric_psd(C_low)
   631	    xin = np.asarray(x_high, dtype=float); xfr = np.asarray(x_low_frozen, dtype=float)
   632	    proj = M @ xin
   633	    require(proj.shape == xfr.shape, f"projected central shape {proj.shape} != frozen {xfr.shape}")
   634	    denom = np.where(np.abs(xfr) > 0, np.abs(xfr), 1.0)
   635	    rel = float(np.max(np.abs(proj - xfr) / denom))
   636	    require(rel <= rtol_central, f"projection mutates central (max rel {rel:.2e})")
   637	    stats["central_max_rel"] = rel
   638	    return C_low, stats

   198	# REPAIR-4 (verifier defect 3b/3c, and KNOWN_ISSUES #23). These used to hash the WORKING TREE
   199	# (`git hash-object <path>`), so the manifest recorded whatever happened to be checked out --

   202	# Now: hash the COMMITTED object at HEAD, record the commit that introduced that exact blob,
   203	# and fail closed if the working tree differs from HEAD for any bound path -- because a
   204	# provenance record that can disagree with what actually ran is worse than none.
   205	def _committed_blob(rel):
   206	    """The blob sha of `rel` as committed at HEAD (not the working-tree copy)."""
   207	    try:
   208	        return subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", f"HEAD:{rel}"],
   209	                                       cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
   210	    except Exception:
   211	        return None
   212	def _worktree_blob(rel):
   213	    try:
   214	        return subprocess.check_output(["git", "hash-object", rel],
   215	                                       cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
   216	    except Exception:

   218	def _blob_introducing_commit(rel, blob):
   219	    """The most recent commit whose version of `rel` IS `blob`. The old code recorded
   220	    `git log -1 -- <rel>`, i.e. the last commit to touch the path, which need not be the commit
   221	    that introduced the blob it recorded beside it."""
   222	    if not blob:
   223	        return None
   224	    try:
   225	        revs = subprocess.check_output(["git", "log", "--format=%H", "--", rel],
   226	                                       cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).split()
   227	        for r in revs:
   228	            try:
   229	                b = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", f"{r}:{rel}"],
   230	                                            cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
   231	            except Exception:
   232	                continue
   233	            if b == blob:
   234	                return r
   235	    except Exception:
   236	        pass
   237	    return None

    47	  local OUT="${OUTDIR}/5d_xsec_MEFHC_5iter_lgbm_uni_full_${tag}.root"
    48	  local REC="${OUT}.done"
    49	  # D2a: the skip is now CONTENT-validating. A ROOT plus any nonempty .done used to be enough;
    50	  # p4_check_receipt.py re-derives root/central/config/bkg_mode identities live and compares the
    51	  # merged sha against the orchestrator receipt. A reject falls through and re-runs the endpoint.
    52	  if [[ -s "${OUT}" && -s "${REC}" ]] && valid_root "${OUT}"; then

    56	    fi
    57	    echo "[unfold] STALE ${tag} -> re-running: ${RCHK}"
    58	    rm -f "${REC}"                       # D2: never leave a stale ROOT/receipt pair behind
    59	  fi

    62	    # was permanently less provable than a produced one. It now carries the same fields.
    63	    local AMH ACH

    68	      "${tag}" "$(sha "${OUT}")" "${AMH}" "${ACH}" "${CFG_HASH}" "${BKG_MODE}" "${CODE_REV}" "${UNFOLD_BLOB}" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > "${REC}.tmp" && mv -f "${REC}.tmp" "${REC}"; }; then
    69	      echo "[unfold] FAIL ${tag} attest receipt publication failed"; rm -f "${REC}.tmp"; return 7
    70	    fi
    71	    echo "[unfold] ATTEST ${tag} (legacy ROOT sha256 == manifest)"; return 0
    72	  fi
    73	  [[ ! -s "${MERGED}" ]] && { echo "[unfold] ABORT ${tag} merged missing"; return 3; }
    74	  local TMP="${OUT}.$$.${RANDOM}.tmp.root"

    82	    # D2c: this used to be an unchecked `printf … && mv`, so a failed receipt write still fell
    83	    # through to `echo DONE` and returned 0 -- a published ROOT with no receipt, reported as
    84	    # success. The write is now the function's success condition.
    85	    if ! { printf '{"tag":"%s","mode":"produced","root_sha256":"%s","merged_sha256":"%s","central5d_sha256":"%s","config_hash":"%s","bkg_mode":"%s","bkg_mode_basis":"passed explicitly to the driver by this launcher","code_rev":"%s","unfold_blob":"%s","t":"%s"}\n' \
    86	      "${tag}" "${RH}" "${MH}" "${CH}" "${CFG_HASH}" "${BKG_MODE}" "${CODE_REV}" "${UNFOLD_BLOB}" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > "${REC}.tmp" && mv -f "${REC}.tmp" "${REC}"; }; then
    87	      echo "[unfold] FAIL ${tag} receipt publication failed after ROOT publish"; rm -f "${REC}.tmp"; return 8
    88	    fi
    89	    echo "[unfold] DONE ${tag}"

    92	  fi

    99	done; done

   107	done; done
   108	# D2d: the loop above only asks whether the ten EXPECTED tags exist, so an eleventh product in
   109	# the directory was invisible to it. Reject extras as well as missing -- an unexplained endpoint
   110	# in a publication namespace is exactly the state this lane spent three weeks in.
   111	extras=0
   112	LIVE_TAGS=$(ls "${OUTDIR}"/5d_xsec_MEFHC_5iter_lgbm_uni_full_*.root 2>/dev/null \
   113	  | sed -e 's#.*uni_full_##' -e 's#\.root$##' | sort)

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Endpoint-receipt gate for run_p4_unfold_std.sh's resume path (repair-4, verifier defect 2).
     3	
     4	Exit 0 iff the receipt is complete and every recorded identity matches the live/committed one;
     5	otherwise print `RECEIPT-REJECT :: <reason>` and exit 1, which makes the launcher re-run the
     6	endpoint transactionally instead of skipping it.
     7	
     8	Deliberately a separate CLI rather than inline `python3 -c` in the launcher: the previous skip
     9	logic was an unreadable one-liner, and a gate that cannot be unit-tested is the defect this
    10	whole repair round exists to remove. ROOT-free -- content validity of the ROOT itself is the
    11	launcher's `valid_root`, this is the provenance half.
    12	
    13	Usage:
    14	  p4_check_receipt.py --receipt R.done --tag BAND_EP --root OUT.root --merged MERGED.root
    15	"""
    16	import argparse, json, os, sys
    17	
    18	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    19	import p4_lib as P
    20	
    21	REPO = P.REPO_ROOT
    22	ND = P.ND_ROOT
    23	CEN5 = f"{ND}/products/5d/xsec_5d_MEFHC_5iter_lgbm.root"
    24	RECDIR = f"{REPO}/docs/orchestration/state/merged-input-hashes/p4-merged-20260718"
    25	UNFOLD_SRC = "nd-unfolding/unfold_nd_omnifold_unbinned.py"
    26	
    27	
    28	def committed_unfold_blob():
    29	    """The unfold driver's blob AS COMMITTED at HEAD (repair-5, defect 2).
    30	
    31	    The receipt gate previously required `code_rev` to be a non-empty string and compared it to
    32	    nothing, and recorded no source identity at all -- so an endpoint produced under a changed
    33	    driver was still skipped. Both are now compared, and this is the value they compare against.
    34	    Fails closed (returns None -> caller rejects) rather than guessing."""
    35	    import subprocess
    36	    try:
    37	        return subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", f"HEAD:{UNFOLD_SRC}"],
    38	                                       cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
    39	    except Exception:
    40	        return None
    41	
    42	
    43	def current_code_rev():
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    try:
    46	        return subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    47	                                       cwd=REPO, text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
    48	    except Exception:
    49	        return None
    50	
    51	
    52	def committed_merged_sha(merged_path):
    53	    """The orchestrator receipt's committed hash for this merged file, after its own live
    54	    size+integer-mtime check. Never re-hashes 53.8 GB."""
    55	    live = {}
    56	    for b in P.BANDS:
    57	        for ep in P.ENDPOINTS:
    58	            rel = (f"nd-unfolding/active_universe_5d/standard/merged/"
    59	                   f"runEventLoopOmniFold_5D_MEFHC_active_{b}_{ep}.root")
    60	            ap = f"{REPO}/{rel}"
    61	            st = os.stat(ap)
    62	            live[rel] = (st.st_size, int(st.st_mtime))
    63	    rec = P.validate_orchestrator_merged_receipt(RECDIR, live)
    64	    base = os.path.basename(merged_path)
    65	    for p, h in rec["merged_sha256"].items():
    66	        if os.path.basename(p) == base:
    67	            return h
    68	    raise P.P4GateError(f"{base} not in the orchestrator merged receipt")
    69	
    70	
    71	def main():
    72	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    73	    ap.add_argument("--receipt", required=True)
    74	    ap.add_argument("--tag", required=True)
    75	    ap.add_argument("--root", required=True)
    76	    ap.add_argument("--merged", required=True)
    77	    a = ap.parse_args()
    78	    try:
    79	        if not os.path.exists(a.receipt) or os.path.getsize(a.receipt) == 0:
    80	            raise P.P4GateError("receipt absent or empty")
    81	        try:
    82	            rec = json.load(open(a.receipt))
    83	        except Exception as e:
    84	            raise P.P4GateError(f"receipt is not valid JSON ({e})")
    85	        cfg = P.P4Config(); cfg.validate()
    86	        blob, rev = committed_unfold_blob(), current_code_rev()
    87	        if not blob:
    88	            raise P.P4GateError(f"cannot resolve the committed blob of {UNFOLD_SRC}; refusing to "
    89	                                f"accept a receipt whose producing source cannot be checked")
    90	        if not rev:
    91	            raise P.P4GateError("cannot resolve HEAD; refusing to accept a receipt whose "
    92	                                "code_rev cannot be compared")
    93	        P.validate_endpoint_receipt(
    94	            rec, tag=a.tag,
    95	            root_sha256=P.sha256_file(a.root),
    96	            merged_sha256=committed_merged_sha(a.merged),
    97	            central5d_sha256=P.sha256_file(CEN5),
    98	            config_hash=cfg.hash(),
    99	            bkg_mode=cfg.bkg_mode,
   100	            code_rev=rev,
   101	            unfold_blob=blob)
   102	    except P.P4GateError as e:
   103	        print(f"RECEIPT-REJECT :: {e}"); sys.exit(1)
   104	    except Exception as e:                      # never let an unexpected error read as PASS
   105	        print(f"RECEIPT-REJECT :: unexpected {type(e).__name__}: {e}"); sys.exit(1)
   106	    print(f"RECEIPT-OK :: {a.tag}")
   107	    sys.exit(0)
   108	
   109	
   110	if __name__ == "__main__":
   111	    main()

     2	# CANONICAL standard-only P4 driver (repair 2026-07-18) — the ONE authoritative,

     5	# FPS post-processing is Agent C's and is never invoked here.
     6	#
     7	# Ordered stages (each fail-closed; the chain aborts on any nonzero stage):
     8	#   1 audit          run_p4_merge_audit_std.sh            (10 hadd + per-playlist audit)
     9	#   2 unfold         run_p4_unfold_std.sh                 (atomic, resumable, --seed 42, no --universe)
    10	#   3 evidence       p4_evidence.py                       (recompute hashes + merged/endpoint receipts + manifest)
    11	#   --- HARD GATE: standard-p4-verifier must PASS on the committed patch before covariance ---
    12	#   4 components     p4_build_components.py               (manifest-bound; named bkgaware components + 5 active bands)
    13	#   5 validate       p4_validate_active_lateral.py        (candidate/support/manifest/merged-audit)

    15	#
    16	# REPAIR-4, 2026-08-07 (verifier defect 1 of six; see
    17	# docs/orchestration/REPAIR4-DEFECT-STATUS-20260807.md). Stages 4-6 had NEVER EXECUTED --
    18	# STOP_AFTER defaulted to a pre-covariance stage, so nothing ever ran them and nothing
    19	# tested them. They were not a working path with typos; all three of the following were
    20	# independently wrong and fixing only the argument names would still have died on the key:
    21	#   (a) ORDER: evidence ran BEFORE unfold, so the manifest described endpoints that the very
    22	#       next stage could rewrite. Correct order is merge+audit -> unfold -> endpoint-evidence,
    23	#       which is now what runs. NOTE the resume/attest path in run_p4_unfold_std.sh reads the
    24	#       COMMITTED manifest from the previous round, which is what legacy attestation means --

    27	#       `--candidate --support --manifest --merged-audit --out`. The projector was called with

    35	#
    36	# STOP_AFTER controls the last stage to run. DEFAULT IS 'audit' -- changed in repair-4 from
    37	# 'evidence', because reordering put `unfold` (which WRITES receipts) before evidence, and a
    38	# default that silently starts writing receipts is the opposite of a safe preflight. Valid:
    39	#   audit | unfold | evidence | components | validate | project
